jobs.title: Executive Director of Advancement Communications
jobs.description:
Caltech is a world-renowned science and engineering institute that marshals some of the world's brightest minds and most innovative tools to address fundamental scientific questions. We thrive on finding and cultivating talented people who are passionate about what they do. Join us and be a part of the diverse Caltech community.

Job Summary

The purpose of Advancement and Alumni Relations (AAR) is to foster a thriving and engaged community of support for Caltech. By strengthening and nurturing the community of people who share and support the Institute's mission and values, we will ensure the Institute receives the necessary resources to achieve our aspirations and advocate for excellence in teaching, research, and scholarship in perpetuity.

Reporting to the Assistant Vice President for Philanthropic Initiatives and Stewardship, the Executive Director of Advancement Communications works closely with the Vice President for Advancement and Alumni Relations and senior leadership. The Executive Director will oversee the strategy, planning and implementation of all marketing and communications efforts to support AAR’s philanthropic and engagement priorities. As AAR’s lead communications strategist, the Executive Director will ensure a consistent voice and visual branding across the organization, with the responsibility for the development of philanthropic messages ranging from fundraising case statements to complex proposals to donor and impact stories disseminated via digital, print, multimedia, and social media platforms. In addition, the Executive Director will drive marketing and earned media strategies that broaden support and engagement by demonstrating the impact of donor philanthropy in support of Caltech’s unparalleled teaching and research mission.

Essential Job Duties

In consultation with advancement leadership, develop, implement, and monitor all philanthropy-related communications, donor storytelling, content strategy, and digital marketing and communications plans to support diverse fundraising initiatives for target audiences through a multi-channel approach that drives engagement and participation.
Lead, mentor, and support a team of two other communications professionals who develop gift announcements, impact stories, social medial posts, videos, newsletters, endowment reports, proposals, cases for support, pitch decks, and other resources that engage individuals with the potential to make annual, major and transformative gifts.
Supervise day-to-day staff assignments, maintaining a balanced workflow to meet deadlines while supporting positive team development. Review all work products to ensure alignment with AAR and Caltech style guidelines, needs, and priorities.
Ensure the publication goal of approximately 40 gift announcements and impact stories is met each year, along with related emails and social media posts.
Produce and/or manage Advancement Communications’ production of proposals and case statements, working directly with frontline fundraisers and faculty.
Manage the strategic use of external partners such as freelance writers, consultants, firms, photographers, designers, and temporary staff.
Serve as an executive communications resource to the Vice President and other advancement leaders, helping to shape strategic initiatives and communications; as needed, develop presentations, talking points and/or remarks for the Vice President.
Establish strategy and relationships with local, state, and national media outlets to amplify gift announcements and philanthropic impact on innovation, research and teaching at Caltech to the general public.
Provide both strategic and hands-on production-level work, effectively serving as a consultant/marketing agency to AAR departments.
Develop processes to evaluate the effectiveness of projects to support continuous improvement and creativity.
Work collaboratively with Alumni Relations, Annual Giving, Caltech Associates, Stewardship, Gift Planning, and other teams that produce their own communications to support the dissemination of key messages.
Oversee the strategy, content management, and regular updating of AAR’s giving and student initiative websites.
Supervise the maintenance of the AAR digital asset management system.
Oversee monthly communications calendar meetings to promote visibility and collaboration among teams that produce AAR communications and to ensure communications are scheduled in a complementary manner.
Plan and lead the AAR Communications Roundtable, a forum for communicators across AAR to connect, share successes and lessons learned, and support consistent and cohesive messaging and branding throughout the division.
Update the AAR Communications Guidelines as needed and ensure all AAR communicators are aware of and follow them. Ensure that AAR communications complement Institute communications and incorporate branding and identity guidelines, as well as tone and voice standards.
Design and conduct workshops for AAR staff to enhance their writing skills, case statement development, proposal writing, reading and writing for content, editing and proofreading.
Manage Advancement Communications’ proofreading and copyediting support for colleagues throughout AAR.
Under the direction of the Vice President, collaborate with the Office of Communications and External Relations on selected institutional projects.
Serve on AAR manager’s team, participating in organizational planning to meet fiscal year operating goals and priorities and facilitating strategic communications across the division.
Establish and monitor team and individual work plans and create supportive and targeted professional development plans for individual team members.
Manage the Advancement Communications budget and prepare proposed budget for each new fiscal year.
Stay abreast of industry trends and conduct best practice reviews of communications at other universities to ensure that Caltech continues as a leader amongst its peers.
Execute other duties as assigned.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor's degree or equivalent work experience with seven or more years of experience in marketing or communications to include developing and executing high-level marketing and communications plans.
Proven experience leading fundraising communications, marketing, and creative services team(s).
Experience developing marketing/communications plans for a major fundraising campaign.
Experience creating a variety of audience-centric communications materials and familiarity with brand and identity development, integrated communications programs, digital communications, and effective graphic design.
Expertise in core marketing principles, strategies, best practices, and communications channels.
Excellent writing and presentation skills.
Excellent organizational and planning skills.
Proven ability to bring discipline and organization to the work while being flexible and responsive to emerging needs.
Proven track record managing personnel, programs, and budgets.
Comprehensive knowledge of every step in the communication and marketing materials production process to guide staff, outside vendors and colleagues in creating outstanding products.
Ability to inspire others, foster cross-divisional collaboration, and manage by influence across a diverse organization.
Ability to give guidance, share and receive constructive feedback, and integrate varying points of view.
Ability to set priorities, meet deadlines, and juggle multiple demands in a complex and fast-paced work environment.
The highest standards of professional and personal conduct; excellent judgment and the ability to treat confidential information with discretion.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook).
Authentic curiosity about science and technology, and an appreciation for the extraordinary intellectual accomplishments and contributions of Caltech donors, faculty, students, alumni, and volunteers.
Demonstrate the ability to practice and adhere to AAR’s Guiding Principles.

Preferred Qualifications

Science, medical, or technical writing/communications experience.
Advanced degree in a communications-intensive discipline.
Experience in higher education.
Recognized (via awards, publications, etc.) by peers for excellence in advancement communications.
Experience with social media platforms, SEO, and GEO.
Proficiency using marketing automation platforms (such as Encompass) and content management systems (such as Wagtail).

Required Documents

Resume
Cover Letter

Hiring Range

$175,100 - $255,000 per year

The salary of the finalist(s) selected for this role will be set based on a variety of factors, including but not limited to, internal equity, experience, education, specialty and training.

As one of the largest employers in Pasadena, CA, Caltech is committed to providing comprehensive benefits to eligible employees and their eligible dependents. Our benefits package includes competitive compensation, health, dental, and vision insurance, retirement savings plans, generous paid time off (vacation, holidays, sick time, parental leave, bereavement, etc.), tuition reimbursement, and more. jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
The Executive Director is the steady hand that sets the direction for everything we do. This is a leader who inspires a team, grows the reach of our hospice care, and makes sure that every patient and family we serve receives the kind of care that reflects who they are and what matters to them most.

This is not an easy role, and it isn't meant to be. Delivering compassion the right way takes skill, heart, commitment, and structure, and it takes a strong leader to hold all four together. Our clinical team is skilled, compassionate, and committed, and they deserve a leader who will champion them, challenge them, and help them grow. Leadership here isn't about who's in your circle or who you already know. It's about leading the way with integrity, solving problems head-on, earning trust, and building a culture where accountability and respect go hand in hand.

At the heart of this role is a true partnership with our clinical leadership. Together, you'll hold the team, and each other, accountable to the highest standard of care. That standard shows up everywhere: in quality outcomes, in the experience families describe when they talk about us, and in a program that is always survey-ready because doing it right is simply how we operate.

Everyone needs a business model, and ours runs on compassionate teamwork. You'll own the operational and financial health of the site, make thoughtful decisions about resources, and build a team people want to join and stay with. Growing our census means building real relationships with physicians, hospitals, facilities, and community partners so that more families can reach us when they need us most, because nobody should die alone.

Crossroads exists because compassion should not be a transaction. Death is a meaningful experience for patients and their loved ones, and we only have one chance to get it right. We aren't blind to the challenges in this industry, but we believe those challenges shouldn't change the heart of our organization; they should make us stronger as a team.

If you are a leader who is energized by a challenge, driven to grow, and ready to prove that this industry can be better, we need you.

Executive Director Core Requirements & Responsibilities:

Master’s Degree in Health Services Administration or closely related field preferred
Bachelor’s Degree considered with extensive applicable experience
3-5 years of leadership experience in healthcare preferably in hospice
Must be able to demonstrate an effective form of communication, professionalism, and organizational skills
Requires the ability to travel
Must have reliable vehicle/transportation, valid driver’s license, required automobile insurance, and the ability to safely and independently operate said vehicle
Working knowledge of hospice regulations, including CMS Conditions of Participation and state licensure requirements
Experience managing a budget or P&L and making data-informed operational decisions
Strong business development and relationship-building skills
The courage to hold high standards and the heart to lead with compassion
Lead the full operations of the site with strong, consistent leadership, setting the tone for a culture built on compassion, accountability, and respect
Partner closely with clinical leadership to hold the team, and each other, accountable to the highest standard of patient care
Grow census by building and maintaining strong relationships with physicians, hospitals, skilled nursing and assisted living facilities, and community partners
Own the operational and financial health of the site, including budget management, resource planning, and sound decision-making that supports sustainable growth
Ensure ongoing compliance with CMS Conditions of Participation, state regulations, and accreditation standards so the program is always survey-ready
Recruit, develop, and retain a skilled interdisciplinary team, creating an environment where people want to join and stay
Solve problems head-on, address challenges directly, and have honest conversations when they matter most
Represent Crossroads in the community as an advocate for hospice care and compassionate end-of-life support

Executive Director Benefits:

Be part of a team willing to grow, listen, be heard, and be challenged
Health, Dental, Vision, 401k, PTO
Set the industry bar for the standard of care
Ability to grow into a variety of different roles inside our team and organization
Competitive Industry pay

jobs.title: Director of Operations
jobs.description:
About the Opportunity

The organization is seeking a full-time, 100% remote Director of Operations
to lead and scale its operations department. Reporting directly to the Chief Operating Officer, this senior leadership position is critical to organizational growth and financial health. The Director of Operations will drive strategic operations, lead a high-performing team, and partner with executive leadership across the organization to ensure operational excellence and sound financial governance.

The ideal candidate combines strategic thinking with hands-on execution, brings fiscal discipline and analytical rigor to complex decisions, and excels at building trust and alignment across teams while navigating ambiguity in a mission-driven nonprofit environment.

Key Responsibilities

Human Resources & Talent Management:
Design and implement hiring processes that attract and retain top talent.
Guide salary negotiations.
Partner with managers to manage staff performance and assist with team development.
Oversee annual performance review processes and training programs for managers.
Integrate organizational core values into all stages of the employee life cycle.
Review benefits structures, recommend updates, and oversee benefits administration.
Own the organization's compensation philosophy and structure.
Manage payroll systems and ensure tax and regulatory requirements are met.
Oversee contract labor acquisition, maintain contractor records, and report on key contractor metrics.

Finance, Budget & Financial Leadership:
Develop and maintain financial dashboards tracking key metrics.
Produce monthly financial reports translating data into actionable insights and strategic implications.
Monitor financial health and proactively flag risks and opportunities.
Build financial models to evaluate ROI on expansion initiatives and strategic investments before implementation.
Lead annual budget development.
Develop rolling cash flow forecasts and scenario models to inform reserve strategy and proactive financial decision-making.
Oversee all financial operations, including accounting, payroll, accounts payable/receivable, cash management, and financial compliance.

Compliance, Legal & Risk Management:
Maintain state and federal compliance, proactively identifying new legal and regulatory requirements.
Maintain workers' compensation policies at national and state levels, ensuring no lapses in required registrations or insurance.
Coordinate FMLA, ADA, and other compliance-related processes, identifying new laws that may impact the organization.
Manage legal claims and lawsuits, coordinating with outside counsel on contract reviews and personnel matters.
Maintain organizational insurance policies and make recommendations on coverage adjustments.

Department Leadership & Administration:
Mentor, coach, and develop operations department personnel.
Schedule and facilitate departmental meetings and oversee annual and quarterly goals.
Maintain organizational systems and tools, managing user access and permissions across platforms.
Supervise the planning of board meetings and coordinate in-person team meetings.

Required Qualifications

5+ years of experience in operations, finance, human resources, or a related field within a nonprofit, mission-driven, or fast-growing organization.
Demonstrated expertise in financial management, budgeting, forecasting, and cash flow analysis.
Strong understanding of and experience in human resources, talent management, and organizational development.
Knowledge of nonprofit compliance, employment law, and risk management.
Demonstrated ability to lead, mentor, and develop high-performing teams in a remote environment.
Strategic thinking skills combining analytical rigor with practical problem-solving and proactive decision-making.
Excellent communication skills with the ability to articulate complex concepts clearly and build alignment across teams.
Comfort with ambiguity and the ability to navigate change in a fast-moving nonprofit environment.
Deep commitment to the organization's mission and a demonstrated ability to exemplify organizational values.
Experience with Google Workspace, Slack, and project management tools.
A computer with reliable internet access.

Preferred Qualifications

Interest in or experience with artificial intelligence tools.
Familiarity with Asana.

Work Environment

This is a full-time, 100% remote position based in the United States, with work conducted from a home office. The organization provides a flexible work environment with flexible scheduling.

Compensation and Benefits

The starting pay range for this role is $120,000–$135,000
, commensurate with experience.
In addition to base salary, the organization offers an annual benefits stipend of $8,000, paid in equal increments in each paycheck once an employee becomes benefits-eligible. The stipend may be applied toward a benefits package—including health, vision, and dental insurance, and retirement accounts—or, if benefits are not elected, received as taxable regular income added to salary. The organization also provides flexible paid time off.

Work Authorization

The organization participates in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with Form I-9 information to confirm authorization to work in the United States. If E-Verify cannot confirm work authorization, the organization is required to provide written instructions and an opportunity to contact the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) or Social Security Administration (SSA) to resolve the issue before taking any adverse action, including termination of employment. E-Verify is used only after a job offer has been accepted and Form I-9 has been completed.

jobs.title: Managing Director, Utility-Scale Solar and Storage Development
jobs.description:
The Company

Our client develops community- and utility-scale solar and battery storage projects across the U.S., leveraging the expertise and national presence of an established real estate investment and development firm with billions of dollars in assets under management.

Role Overview

Our client seeks a Managing Director to expand its utility-scale solar and storage portfolio, enter new markets, and steer projects from origination through funding and construction. This executive will oversee fundraising, financial evaluation, and capital allocation while advising the wider renewables team, including distributed generation. Texas or Washington, DC is preferred, with other U.S. locations considered.

Duties & Responsibilities

Shape our client’s expansion plans for large-scale solar and battery assets, offering expertise to the distributed generation team when needed
Guide projects from land sourcing and securing property rights through grid connection, approvals, environmental reviews, technical design, revenue agreements, funding, notice to proceed, and construction
Direct progress across the battery project backlog, particularly assets navigating PJM’s grid connection queue
Assess prospective regions and investments, using grid access, policy, revenue potential, and financial viability to determine entry plans
Grow the project portfolio through new site origination, asset purchases, joint ventures, and strategic alliances
Determine which projects merit funding by weighing execution uncertainty, cash needs, profitability, timelines, and anticipated returns
Coordinate with colleagues and outside counterparties to secure buyers and establish routes to market
Attract funding for the business and its assets from institutional backers, banks, and strategic investors
Work with executives on funding arrangements, ownership structures, financial assessments, investment approval submissions, and business priorities
Cultivate connections with power providers, grid operators, property owners, public agencies, advisers, project sponsors, and financial partners
Introduce workflows, milestone reviews, spending plans, delivery timelines, and controls that support measured expansion
Hire, coach, and strengthen the solar and storage team as the business grows
Deliver recommendations on assets, funding, and business direction to executives and relevant decision-makers
Act as our client’s representative with financial backers, business partners, and industry groups to uncover new opportunities

Qualifications

Undergraduate degree required; postgraduate qualifications preferred
At least fifteen years developing clean energy, electricity, or infrastructure assets, with substantial expertise in large-scale solar and battery systems
Proven success moving major energy assets through successive milestones, preferably from initial origination to construction authorization, funding, buildout, and operational launch
Comprehensive knowledge of land rights, grid access, approvals, environmental assessments, technical design, financial feasibility, revenue arrangements, and funding
History of establishing, expanding, or directing a major renewables business or substantial asset portfolio
Thorough understanding of U.S. electricity markets and regional grid operators; direct PJM grid connection experience is essential for our client’s active projects, with exposure to ERCOT, CAISO, MISO, and SPP highly desirable
Skill in turning policy, market conditions, grid constraints, and revenue prospects into practical expansion plans
Substantial experience securing project funding and attracting capital, with the standing to work effectively with institutional backers and lending partners
Sound investment judgment across financial modeling, execution risks, funding needs, and projected returns, including delivering proposals to investment approval panels
Working knowledge of distributed generation sufficient to advise our client’s team; the position primarily centers on larger-scale assets
Initiative and commercial drive to set direction and deliver results within an expanding business
Credible executive leadership, persuasive communication, effective dealmaking, and strong professional relationships

jobs.title: Chief Operating Officer
jobs.description:
Role Description
This full-time remote Chief Operating Officer role is responsible for overseeing day-to-day business operations and driving organizational performance. The COO will lead operational planning, set measurable goals, and ensure alignment between strategy, processes, and resources across all departments. This role includes designing and improving workflows, monitoring key performance indicators, and implementing best practices for efficiency, quality, and compliance. The COO will collaborate closely with the executive team on long-term business planning, financial sustainability, and risk management, while mentoring leaders and fostering a culture of accountability, transparency, and continuous improvement. The role also involves managing budgets, optimizing resource allocation, and using data-driven insights to support decision-making and sustainable growth.
Qualifications

Strong business planning and strategic leadership skills, with experience translating organizational vision into executable roadmaps.
Proficiency in operations management, including process optimization, performance measurement, and cross-functional coordination.
Robust analytical skills, with the ability to interpret data, develop insights, and support evidence-based decision-making.
Solid finance and budgeting capabilities, including managing P&L, forecasting, and resource allocation.
Proven experience in an executive or senior operations role, ideally within a growing or complex organization.
Excellent communication, collaboration, and stakeholder management skills across diverse teams and levels.
Demonstrated ability to lead remote teams, build trust, and sustain engagement in a distributed work environment.
Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, Operations, or a related field; an advanced degree (e.g., MBA) is beneficial.
Commitment to inclusive leadership, ethical decision-making, and cultivating a non-discriminatory workplace.

new_jobs.description:
About the Opportunity

The organization is seeking a full-time, 100% remote Director of Operations
to lead and scale its operations department. Reporting directly to the Chief Operating Officer, this senior leadership position is critical to organizational growth and financial health. The Director of Operations will drive strategic operations, lead a high-performing team, and partner with executive leadership across the organization to ensure operational excellence and sound financial governance.

The ideal candidate combines strategic thinking with hands-on execution, brings fiscal discipline and analytical rigor to complex decisions, and excels at building trust and alignment across teams while navigating ambiguity in a mission-driven nonprofit environment.

Key Responsibilities

Human Resources & Talent Management:
Design and implement hiring processes that attract and retain top talent.
Guide salary negotiations.
Partner with managers to manage staff performance and assist with team development.
Oversee annual performance review processes and training programs for managers.
Integrate organizational core values into all stages of the employee life cycle.
Review benefits structures, recommend updates, and oversee benefits administration.
Own the organization's compensation philosophy and structure.
Manage payroll systems and ensure tax and regulatory requirements are met.
Oversee contract labor acquisition, maintain contractor records, and report on key contractor metrics.

Finance, Budget & Financial Leadership:
Develop and maintain financial dashboards tracking key metrics.
Produce monthly financial reports translating data into actionable insights and strategic implications.
Monitor financial health and proactively flag risks and opportunities.
Build financial models to evaluate ROI on expansion initiatives and strategic investments before implementation.
Lead annual budget development.
Develop rolling cash flow forecasts and scenario models to inform reserve strategy and proactive financial decision-making.
Oversee all financial operations, including accounting, payroll, accounts payable/receivable, cash management, and financial compliance.

Compliance, Legal & Risk Management:
Maintain state and federal compliance, proactively identifying new legal and regulatory requirements.
Maintain workers' compensation policies at national and state levels, ensuring no lapses in required registrations or insurance.
Coordinate FMLA, ADA, and other compliance-related processes, identifying new laws that may impact the organization.
Manage legal claims and lawsuits, coordinating with outside counsel on contract reviews and personnel matters.
Maintain organizational insurance policies and make recommendations on coverage adjustments.

Department Leadership & Administration:
Mentor, coach, and develop operations department personnel.
Schedule and facilitate departmental meetings and oversee annual and quarterly goals.
Maintain organizational systems and tools, managing user access and permissions across platforms.
Supervise the planning of board meetings and coordinate in-person team meetings.

Required Qualifications

5+ years of experience in operations, finance, human resources, or a related field within a nonprofit, mission-driven, or fast-growing organization.
Demonstrated expertise in financial management, budgeting, forecasting, and cash flow analysis.
Strong understanding of and experience in human resources, talent management, and organizational development.
Knowledge of nonprofit compliance, employment law, and risk management.
Demonstrated ability to lead, mentor, and develop high-performing teams in a remote environment.
Strategic thinking skills combining analytical rigor with practical problem-solving and proactive decision-making.
Excellent communication skills with the ability to articulate complex concepts clearly and build alignment across teams.
Comfort with ambiguity and the ability to navigate change in a fast-moving nonprofit environment.
Deep commitment to the organization's mission and a demonstrated ability to exemplify organizational values.
Experience with Google Workspace, Slack, and project management tools.
A computer with reliable internet access.

Preferred Qualifications

Interest in or experience with artificial intelligence tools.
Familiarity with Asana.

Work Environment

This is a full-time, 100% remote position based in the United States, with work conducted from a home office. The organization provides a flexible work environment with flexible scheduling.

Compensation and Benefits

The starting pay range for this role is $120,000–$135,000
, commensurate with experience.
In addition to base salary, the organization offers an annual benefits stipend of $8,000, paid in equal increments in each paycheck once an employee becomes benefits-eligible. The stipend may be applied toward a benefits package—including health, vision, and dental insurance, and retirement accounts—or, if benefits are not elected, received as taxable regular income added to salary. The organization also provides flexible paid time off.

Work Authorization

The organization participates in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with Form I-9 information to confirm authorization to work in the United States. If E-Verify cannot confirm work authorization, the organization is required to provide written instructions and an opportunity to contact the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) or Social Security Administration (SSA) to resolve the issue before taking any adverse action, including termination of employment. E-Verify is used only after a job offer has been accepted and Form I-9 has been completed.

The Company

Our client develops community- and utility-scale solar and battery storage projects across the U.S., leveraging the expertise and national presence of an established real estate investment and development firm with billions of dollars in assets under management.

Role Overview

Our client seeks a Managing Director to expand its utility-scale solar and storage portfolio, enter new markets, and steer projects from origination through funding and construction. This executive will oversee fundraising, financial evaluation, and capital allocation while advising the wider renewables team, including distributed generation. Texas or Washington, DC is preferred, with other U.S. locations considered.

Duties & Responsibilities

Shape our client’s expansion plans for large-scale solar and battery assets, offering expertise to the distributed generation team when needed
Guide projects from land sourcing and securing property rights through grid connection, approvals, environmental reviews, technical design, revenue agreements, funding, notice to proceed, and construction
Direct progress across the battery project backlog, particularly assets navigating PJM’s grid connection queue
Assess prospective regions and investments, using grid access, policy, revenue potential, and financial viability to determine entry plans
Grow the project portfolio through new site origination, asset purchases, joint ventures, and strategic alliances
Determine which projects merit funding by weighing execution uncertainty, cash needs, profitability, timelines, and anticipated returns
Coordinate with colleagues and outside counterparties to secure buyers and establish routes to market
Attract funding for the business and its assets from institutional backers, banks, and strategic investors
Work with executives on funding arrangements, ownership structures, financial assessments, investment approval submissions, and business priorities
Cultivate connections with power providers, grid operators, property owners, public agencies, advisers, project sponsors, and financial partners
Introduce workflows, milestone reviews, spending plans, delivery timelines, and controls that support measured expansion
Hire, coach, and strengthen the solar and storage team as the business grows
Deliver recommendations on assets, funding, and business direction to executives and relevant decision-makers
Act as our client’s representative with financial backers, business partners, and industry groups to uncover new opportunities

Qualifications

Undergraduate degree required; postgraduate qualifications preferred
At least fifteen years developing clean energy, electricity, or infrastructure assets, with substantial expertise in large-scale solar and battery systems
Proven success moving major energy assets through successive milestones, preferably from initial origination to construction authorization, funding, buildout, and operational launch
Comprehensive knowledge of land rights, grid access, approvals, environmental assessments, technical design, financial feasibility, revenue arrangements, and funding
History of establishing, expanding, or directing a major renewables business or substantial asset portfolio
Thorough understanding of U.S. electricity markets and regional grid operators; direct PJM grid connection experience is essential for our client’s active projects, with exposure to ERCOT, CAISO, MISO, and SPP highly desirable
Skill in turning policy, market conditions, grid constraints, and revenue prospects into practical expansion plans
Substantial experience securing project funding and attracting capital, with the standing to work effectively with institutional backers and lending partners
Sound investment judgment across financial modeling, execution risks, funding needs, and projected returns, including delivering proposals to investment approval panels
Working knowledge of distributed generation sufficient to advise our client’s team; the position primarily centers on larger-scale assets
Initiative and commercial drive to set direction and deliver results within an expanding business
Credible executive leadership, persuasive communication, effective dealmaking, and strong professional relationships
